headline: Executable remediation plan for Helpotron mega-audit extended findings, organized in 4 consequence-ordered waves.

steps.title: Fix shallow merge dropping nested user settings
steps.why_first: Silent user data loss: updating a nested preference like ai.detection.threshold currently obliterates sibling keys like ai.detection.enabled in the JSON settings blob.
steps.change: Replace shallow dictionary .update() in UserSettingsService.update_user_settings with recursive _deep_merge helper that recursively updates dictionaries while preserving sibling properties.

write.name: test_deep_merge_preserves_nested_siblings
write.proves: Updating a sub-key inside a nested dict preserves other pre-existing keys in that same nested dict.
write.body:
def test_deep_merge_preserves_nested_siblings():
    from server.user_settings_service import UserSettingsService
    from server.database import SessionLocal, User
    import uuid
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        user = User(public_id=f'test_user_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}', settings={'ai': {'detection': {'enabled': True, 'threshold': 80}}})
        db.add(user)
        db.commit()
        UserSettingsService.update_user_settings(db, user, {'ai': {'detection': {'threshold': 95}}})
        updated = UserSettingsService.get_user_settings(user)
        assert updated['ai']['detection']['threshold'] == 95
        assert updated['ai']['detection']['enabled'] is True, 'Sibling key enabled was dropped by shallow merge!'
    finally:
        db.close()

steps.done_when: test_deep_merge_preserves_nested_siblings passes and nested keys survive partial updates.
steps.risk: none material; settings updates still go through atomic core UPDATE and preserve REPLACE_ON_WRITE keys.

steps.title: Map public paths and legacy view aliases in App.jsx to prevent blank screens
steps.why_first: Blank screens / navigation dead ends: authed users navigating to /guide, /terms, /privacy, /pricing, or /study get stuck or blank screens because paths are missing from VIEW_PATH_MAP and view keys are unmapped.
steps.change: Add '/guide', '/terms', '/privacy', '/pricing', '/study', and '/features' to VIEW_PATH_MAP, and add aliases in LEGACY_VIEWS for 'pricing', 'study', 'signup', 'features', 'guide', 'terms', 'privacy'.

steps.done_when: App.jsx builds cleanly with zero errors and test_app_routes_coverage passes.
steps.risk: none material; expands routing map without altering existing views.

steps.title: Update draft and transcription task token debit pricing
steps.why_first: Financial loss: draft generations are charged 2.0 tokens ($0.0002) and audio transcription 1 token/hr ($0.0001), 500x-1500x below real compute/upstream API costs.
steps.change: Set DRAFT_COST to 200.0 tokens ($0.02 floor) in server/draft.py, and update audio transcription charge in server/main.py to 500.0 tokens per hour ($0.05 floor) with proper transaction ledger recording.

write.name: test_draft_and_transcription_costs
write.proves: Draft cost is at least 200 tokens ($0.02) and transcription is billed at 500 tokens/hr ($0.05/hr) rather than sub-cent fraction fractions.
write.body:
def test_draft_and_transcription_costs():
    from server.draft import DRAFT_COST
    assert DRAFT_COST >= 200.0, f'DRAFT_COST {DRAFT_COST} is stale'
    with open('server/main.py') as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert 'hours * 500' in content or 'TRANSCRIPTION_TOKEN_RATE' in content or 'hours = max(1.0' in content and '500' in content

steps.done_when: Draft and transcription debit logic uses updated task token floors.
steps.risk: Low; ensures debits cover upstream compute costs.

steps.title: Support path-level scoped settings updates to prevent cross-tab clobbering
steps.why_first: Concurrency data loss: writing any scoped setting completely overwrites the 'scoped' dict, destroying other override paths created in other tabs.
steps.change: When k == 'scoped' in update_user_settings, merge updates per path key (current['scoped'][path] = v[path]) rather than replacing the entire top-level 'scoped' dictionary.

write.name: test_scoped_settings_path_merge
write.proves: Updating a scoped setting for path A preserves pre-existing scoped settings for path B.
write.body:
def test_scoped_settings_path_merge():
    from server.user_settings_service import UserSettingsService
    from server.database import SessionLocal, User
    import uuid
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        user = User(public_id=f'test_user_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}', settings={'scoped': {'path_a': [{'id': '1', 'value': 'val_a'}]}})
        db.add(user)
        db.commit()
        UserSettingsService.update_user_settings(db, user, {'scoped': {'path_b': [{'id': '2', 'value': 'val_b'}]}})
        updated = UserSettingsService.get_user_settings(user)
        assert 'path_a' in updated['scoped'], 'Path A was wiped when Path B was written!'
        assert 'path_b' in updated['scoped']
    finally:
        db.close()

steps.done_when: test_scoped_settings_path_merge passes and independent scoped paths coexist.
steps.risk: none material; allows full dictionary clearing when an empty dictionary is explicitly passed for a path.

steps.title: Sweep stale token tier numbers in web components and enforce with guard test
steps.why_first: False advertising & user confusion: components display old pre-migration figures (150, 300, 1,000, 2,700 tokens) instead of canonical tier allowances (15,000, 30,000, 100,000, 270,000).
steps.change: Update stale tier numbers across JSX components to canonical values (Trial 15,000, Basic 30,000, Pro 100,000, Elite 270,000). Create scripts/check_stale_numbers.js guard test that fails on any stale tier numbers.

write.name: check_stale_numbers
write.proves: No component in web/src contains pre-migration token numbers in token/tier context.

steps.done_when: scripts/check_stale_numbers.js runs and exits with status 0, finding 0 stale token literals.
steps.risk: none material; updates user-facing copy and comments.

steps.title: Correct password hashing and storage claims in SECURITY.md
steps.why_first: Security disclosure integrity: SECURITY.md falsely claims bcrypt and AES-256 at-rest encryption, contradicting actual code (PBKDF2-SHA256 and plaintext SQLite rows).
steps.change: Update SECURITY.md:49-51 to accurately document PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100,000 iterations) and TLS 1.3 transit encryption, removing false AES-256 at-rest claims.

write.name: test_security_md_truthfulness
write.proves: SECURITY.md does not claim bcrypt or AES-256 encryption at rest.
write.body:
def test_security_md_truthfulness():
    with open('SECURITY.md') as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert 'bcrypt' not in content, 'SECURITY.md still falsely claims bcrypt'
    assert 'AES-256' not in content, 'SECURITY.md still falsely claims AES-256 at rest'
    assert 'PBKDF2' in content
    assert 'TLS 1.3' in content

steps.done_when: SECURITY.md truthfully reflects the cryptographic algorithms used in production.

steps.title: Align FERPA and COPPA claims with actual educational data posture
steps.why_first: Compliance risk: product cannot claim official institutional FERPA certification, but must accurately describe student-initiated data import and zero-sale posture.
steps.change: Refine FERPA and COPPA claims to specify that Helpotron is student-initiated and self-service, preserving student privacy rights without false certification claims.

write.name: test_ferpa_coppa_alignment
write.proves: Claims avoid asserting institutional FERPA certification and clearly state student-directed access.
write.body:
def test_ferpa_coppa_alignment():
    with open('SECURITY.md') as f:
        s = f.read()
    assert 'FERPA & COPPA Compliance:' not in s, 'Unsubstantiated certification header in SECURITY.md'
    assert 'Student Privacy & Compliance' in s or 'Student Privacy' in s

steps.done_when: Educational privacy claims are properly contextualized.

steps.title: Offload monitors.py snapshot_once to asyncio.to_thread and throttle history trimming
steps.why_first: Event loop starvation: monitors.py calls sync file/process I/O directly in run_monitors_loop, blocking all concurrent API requests.
steps.change: Wrap snapshot_once() calls in asyncio.to_thread() inside run_monitors_loop, and throttle _trim_history to execute only once every 30 snapshots.

write.name: test_monitors_async_offload
write.proves: run_monitors_loop offloads sync work to worker thread using to_thread.
write.body:
def test_monitors_async_offload():
    with open('server/monitors.py') as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert 'await asyncio.to_thread(snapshot_once)' in content, 'snapshot_once not offloaded via to_thread'

steps.done_when: snapshot_once is awaited via to_thread in the background monitors loop.

steps.title: Gate telegram_agent_loop polling with idle backoff when no bots connected
steps.why_first: CPU waste & SQLite contention: telegram_agent_loop scans the entire User table and parses settings every 3 seconds even with 0 bots connected.
steps.change: When _connected_users() returns an empty list, increase poll interval to 30 seconds to prevent constant SQLite churn.

write.name: test_telegram_link_idle_backoff
write.proves: telegram_agent_loop applies idle backoff when no users have bots connected.
write.body:
def test_telegram_link_idle_backoff():
    with open('server/telegram_agent_link.py') as f:
        content = f.read()
    assert 'IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL' in content or 'sleep(30' in content or 'sleep(IDLE_INTERVAL' in content, 'No idle backoff in telegram loop'

steps.done_when: Idle telegram polling sleeps for 30s instead of querying SQLite every 3s.

steps.change: Fetch all StudyCardState records in a single query with StudyCardState.material_id.in_(material_ids), grouping by material_id in memory.
